# ProviderEnhance
**English** | Chinese

**One third-party provider, many named configurations.** DeepSeek Harness (DSH)
binds one credential

per provider route; ProviderEnhance turns a provider
profile into a container of equally editable c

onfigurations — each with its own
name, API key, endpoint, wire protocol and model list. Chat's mode

l picker
groups models by those configuration names.

> Built and tested against **DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.3** on Windows. The adapter
> half is a patched bu

ild of the bundled `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai`; read
> Compatibility and risks before upgrading DSH

ld of the bundled `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai`; read
> Compatibility and risks before upgrading DSH.
Maintained by Youpeng (@elliotmasheal).
## Screenshots

*The Models page: one provider card holding several peer configurations, each
with its own key, endp
oint, protocol and model list.*

*The chat model picker: models are grouped under configuration names
(`opencode-go-google`, `opencod

cker: models are grouped under configuration names
(`opencode-go-google`, `opencode-go-github`, …).*
## Why

A model route in DSH is one `provider` id with one display name, one credential
reference and one mo

del list; registering the same route twice fails with
`DUPLICATE_ADAPTER`. That makes "two subscript

ions of the same provider"
impossible with the stock UI. ProviderEnhance keeps **one** provider id i

n
configuration and expands its `accounts` into internal routes at load time, so
each configuration

gets its own credential and its own chat group while the
Models page still shows a single provider r

s its own credential and its own chat group while the
Models page still shows a single provider row.
## Install

Requirements: DSH Desktop 0.2.x with the desktop profile, and the Node/pnpm that
DSH ships (the scri

pt finds them). Node 22+ is only needed when you run the
script with your own Node.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The installer:

1. links `packages/adapter` as `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` in the profile, so the
loader resolves t

he patched adapter for the existing `llm-pi-ai` row;
2. links `packages/ui` and appends it to `dsh.p
ml` are written first).

Restart DSH Desktop afterwards. The profile links to this clone, so keep the
directory where it is (
re-run the installer if you move it).
Options:

- `--dry-run` prints the manifest changes without writing them.
- `--no-install` skips pnpm; run `pn

pm install` in the profile yourself.
- `--home <DSH_HOME>` for a non-default harness home.
- `--prof
ile <name>` for a profile other than `desktop`.

The installer edits the profile manifest, so review it with `--dry-run` first if
you keep the profil
e under version control.

The UI bundle is also published on npm as
`dsh-provider-enhance`.
It is only the Web half: the stock

adapter rejects `accounts`, so installing the
npm package alone shows the configuration editor but

breaks provider loading.
The installer above adds both halves; if you install from npm, link
`packag
es/adapter` into the profile as well.
## Use

1. **Settings → Models → Add model provider**, pick a third-party provider
(for example `opencode-go

`) and paste the first subscription's API key.
2. Open that provider's card. Its configurations are

listed collapsed; use
**+ Add configuration** to add the next subscription.
3. Click a configuration

write-only in DSH's credential store;
- **Customized settings** — endpoint, wire protocol, model li

st with
**Fetch models** (catalog lookup for catalog providers, `GET {baseURL}/models`
for custom en

t without touching the provider's name.
4. Chat: the model picker shows one group per configuration

name. The
provider's own product name is only used as the Models-page row title.
## Configuration model
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- `accounts[0]` is served on the base route id (`opencode-go`), so
`agent-default-model` and existin

g session logs keep working; entries 2…N
expand to internal routes `opencode-go#2`, `#3` that inheri

t the profile and
catalog.
- Every configuration of an installed catalog provider — including the ba

se one
— resolves through that catalog. The catalog supplies each known model's
default protocol, en

dpoint, compatibility and metadata; an account's `api` /
`baseURL` win over those defaults when set,

and `models` replaces the served
list. Configurations therefore behave identically instead of confi

guration 1
forcing its own protocol.
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility and risks

- **Pinned to DSH 0.2.1-rc.3.** `packages/adapter/lib/index.js` is a built
artifact extracted from t

hat build and patched. After a DSH upgrade, re-run
the upstream extraction and re-apply the patches

in
docs/upgrading.md; otherwise the plugin fails to load or
loses the accounts feature.
- **The adap

ter overrides the bundled package by name**, which is the only way a
plugin can replace it; this als

o means the override must be re-linked after a
DSH upgrade. The override affects the whole profile,

not only providers that
use configurations.
- **The Models page's per-provider Edit button** is hidd

en for providers with
more than one configuration by a DOM lookup (`*_rowActions`). If a future
buil

d renames that class, the button reappears; nothing else depends on it.
- **The stock Add model prov

ider dropdown** only lists unconfigured providers.
Adding another configuration of an existing provi

der happens inside its card
(`+ Add configuration`); this is a page-internal filter that slots canno

t
extend.
- **Provider profiles created by an older single-provider setup** are not
migrated automat

ically: add a configuration and paste the existing key once.
- **Platform support:** tested on Windo

ws only. The scripts use portable Node
APIs but macOS and Linux are unverified.
- **Security:** the

plugin runs in-process with the user's permissions and
writes to the DSH profile. See SECURITY.md.
This project is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by DeepSeek.
